notes: Box score from Digest Sports' page for the Trail Blazers' 116–94 home win over Golden State on Nov 27, 2026, matched stat for stat by Hoops Nightly: all 116 Portland points and all 94 Golden State points add up from the player lines, as do the shooting totals (41 of 96, 12 of 49 from three, 22 of 23 FT for Portland; 32 of 88, 14 of 42, 16 of 24 for Golden State). The quarter scores (37–30–24–25 to 11–33–34–16) are in both; 67–44 at the half and 91–78 after three are also in Field Level Media and Fastbreak Journal. Points in the paint (58–30), second-chance points (23–14) and points off turnovers (19–14) are from Hoops Nightly; bench points (44–28) are on Hoops Nightly and add up from the box. Portland's biggest lead, 36 (47–11 early in the second quarter), is in Digest Sports, the AP and Field Level Media; Golden State never led. Deni Avdija's 7 rebounds are from both box scores and Basketball-Reference (the AP story says 8). Records are from the site's standings after Friday's games.

Portland scored 20 of the first 23 points (Field Level Media) and led 37–11 after one quarter, when Golden State shot 4 for 24 (AP). The Warriors won the second and third quarters and cut it to 100–90 on Yaxel Lendeborg's driving layup with 5:10 left (AP; Field Level Media), before Portland's 14–0 run to 114–90 (Field Level Media; Fastbreak Journal). Seven Blazers scored in double figures (SI). Stephen Curry (oblique) missed a seventh straight game for Golden State, and Damian Lillard (calf) sat out for Portland (Field Level Media; AP). Portland has won three straight (Hoops Nightly; Field Level Media), won NBA Cup West Group C at 3–1 on a tiebreaker (Field Level Media; SI), and hosts Memphis in the quarterfinals on Dec 5 (AP). The Blazers host New Orleans on Sunday (AP; Hoops Nightly).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Deni Avdija's running layup with 1:05 left, assisted by Scoot Henderson, and the free throw after it: the Digest Sports play-by-play has the layup at 1:05 for 111–90 to 113–90 and the free throw for 114–90, and Fastbreak Journal and Field Level Media describe the same three-point play finishing the 14–0 run. So the board's Blazers +21 to +23 is 111–90 to 113–90 before the free throw. The defender isn't described, so it is drawn as the template's drive to the rim. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Portland Trail Blazers or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The player in the play of the game is drawn to Deni Avdija's listed 6-foot-8 and 228 pounds (Basketball-Reference), with arms at the default length, in the Blazers' home kit with No. 8 (SI; Yahoo Sports), with his proposed look from the site's look sheet. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
